narratives.Description: BLOCKER: bug(build,canon): build and main still mandate xBRIEF 0.6 after #2971
narratives.Overview:
## Summary

Current `master` has a live authoring-contract split after #2971: setup writes xBRIEF 0.8, while the build skill and root `main.md` still issue MUST-level instructions that 0.6 is canonical and every xBRIEF must use 0.6.

This was found in a real greenfield consumer onboarding on Directive 0.105.0 and reproduced against `master` at `522643763423b57d4ca7e9ddb551785d3a2bfb84`.

## Reproduction

1. Complete `deft-directive-setup` for a greenfield project.
2. Setup emits:

   ```json
   { "xBRIEFInfo": { "version": "0.8" } }
   ```

3. Continue to `deft-directive-build` and read its mandatory xBRIEF contract.

## Observed contradiction

Setup correctly says:

- output MUST conform to xBRIEF v0.8 and use strict `const: "0.8"`: [setup skill lines 563-568](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/522643763423b57d4ca7e9ddb551785d3a2bfb84/content/skills/deft-directive-setup/SKILL.md#L563-L568)
- emitting 0.6 on a new write path is forbidden: [setup skill lines 741-746](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/522643763423b57d4ca7e9ddb551785d3a2bfb84/content/skills/deft-directive-setup/SKILL.md#L741-L746)

Build then says the opposite:

> All xBRIEFs ... MUST use `"xBRIEFInfo": { "version": "0.6" }`. The validator rejects any other version.

[Build skill line 237](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/522643763423b57d4ca7e9ddb551785d3a2bfb84/content/skills/deft-directive-build/SKILL.md#L237)

The root framework constitution repeats the obsolete contract:

- `### Schema version: v0.6 (canonical)`
- every vBRIEF MUST emit `vBRIEFInfo.version: 0.6`
- the removed Python validator/migrator is described as canonical

[main.md lines 210-217](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/522643763423b57d4ca7e9ddb551785d3a2bfb84/main.md#L210-L217)

The consumer project definition and proposed story validate as 0.8, but the next required skill tells the agent to reject or rewrite them to 0.6.

## Impact

- A conformant greenfield setup cannot enter build with one coherent schema authority.
- Agents can generate obsolete 0.6 artifacts from a current 0.8 project.
- The strongest loaded prose (`main.md` plus the build skill) contradicts the current writer and schema.
- A consumer can oscillate between "write 0.8" and "0.8 is rejected" depending on which required skill is active.

This is separate from #3598, which covers greenfield specification/export authority and the setup-to-cost loop. It is also outside closed #3555, which fixed render validation. Closed #2971 explicitly required interview/setup/templates/examples to emit 0.8; the build and root constitution residues remain live.

## Expected

Current write paths and live agent instructions should have one rule:

- xBRIEF 0.8 is the only new-write default.
- 0.6 is read/migration compatibility only and must never be taught as the current authoring format.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Build accepts and emits `xBRIEFInfo.version: "0.8"` for current projects.
- [ ] Root `main.md` describes xBRIEF 0.8 as the current write authority; 0.6 appears only in clearly bounded legacy/read/migration guidance.
- [ ] No MUST-level live authoring instruction says new xBRIEFs use 0.6 or that 0.8 is rejected.
- [ ] A content-contract test scans current authoring surfaces (`main.md`, setup, build, interview/templates) for conflicting write-version mandates.
- [ ] A packed-consumer fixture covers `setup -> proposed 0.8 scope -> build preflight` without version disagreement.
- [ ] Existing 0.6 read compatibility remains covered without weakening the 0.8 write default.

## Related

- #2971 — closed write-default repair whose build/main residue remains
- #3555 — closed render-validation repair; not this live authoring contradiction
- #3598 — separate greenfield export/cost authority blocker discovered in the same onboarding

## Issue comment thread

_The issue body is the original write-up; maintainer comments below may supersede it. Read the full thread before building a dispatch envelope (#2143)._

### Comment by @MScottAdams (2026-08-30T04:28:20Z)

**Unsequenced from #3899 by operator decision, 2026-08-29.** This issue no longer waits on the `REFERENCES.md` classification decision and can proceed now.

#3899 round 1 grouped this with #3601 and #3602 as one class — *"the shipped consumer deposit instructs an agent to read files and run helpers the package does not contain"* — and sequenced all three behind a single decision.

Round 2's panel established that the grouping is **by symptom, not by cause**. The three have different mechanisms and therefore different fixes:

| Issue | Mechanism |
|---|---|
| #3601 | a manifest **classification** conflict — `REFERENCES.md` is bucket `repo-dev`, deliberately maintainer-only, while the managed card mandates reading it |
| #3600 | **stale canon** in a file that ships correctly |
| #3602 | **migration residue** in prose after a language port |

Only #3601 turns on the bucket decision. Holding the other two behind it bought nothing and delayed both.

Round 1's sequencing was reasonable on the evidence it had — it ran N=1 and the symptom really is common to all three. Round 2's causal read supersedes it. Full reasoning: critic B `5466142629`, synthesis `5466693576`.

**No change to this issue's own diagnosis or scope.** #3899 explicitly does not re-open or re-cut it; it remains the unit of work. This removes a dependency, nothing else.

One piece of context: **v0.108.0 has shipped**, so this defect is in the released artifact. That makes it post-release remediation rather than a pre-cut blocker — and `blocks-release-tag`, where applied, has no deterministic reader anyway (its only wired consumer is triage-queue ranking, measured by critic A).

Refs #3601, #3602, #3899, #3937.
